title: Real-Time Business Intelligence Analytics Dashboard with Node.js WebSockets, Redis Pub/Sub & PostgreSQL Rollups
problem: Executive and operational teams relying on periodic page refreshes to monitor critical business KPIs suffer from stale metrics, uncoordinated decision-making, and heavy database load from repetitive analytical queries. Polling REST APIs every few seconds exhausts server connection pools and introduces significant latency lag during rapid traffic surges. This project builds a production-grade real-time business intelligence (BI) dashboard in TypeScript and React. The system ingests business transaction events in Node.js, distributes live metric mutations horizontally across worker processes using Redis Pub/Sub, pushes delta updates to thousands of browser clients over WebSockets with sub-35ms broadcast latency, computes historical multi-dimensional rollups in PostgreSQL, and renders interactive SVG/Canvas charts with zero UI stutter.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Black Friday Flash-Sale Monitoring
use_cases.first_sentence: Retail merchandise directors need to monitor live revenue, order volume, and inventory depletion velocity across product categories during flash sales.
use_cases.second_sentence: The dashboard displays real-time ticker updates and conversion rate heatmaps, streaming purchase deltas over WebSockets within 25 milliseconds of order placement.

use_cases.title: FinTech Payment Gateway Transaction & Anomaly Operations
use_cases.first_sentence: Payment platform reliability teams require immediate visualization of payment authorization success rates and fraud decline spikes across banking partners.
use_cases.second_sentence: The streaming dashboard graphs rolling authorization percentages in real time, triggering visual alert banners when gateway error rates exceed defined thresholds.

use_cases.title: SaaS Platform User Activity & Subscription ARR Metrics
use_cases.first_sentence: Executive leadership needs an operational display tracking active user concurrency, plan upgrades, and recurring revenue metrics updated continuously.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system aggregates live billing and activity events in Redis, streaming live ARR and user count updates to executive browser sessions without requiring manual page reloads.

hard_parts: Designing high-throughput WebSocket connection management in Node.js supporting 2,000 concurrent browser sessions with heartbeats and auto-reconnection
Implementing horizontal multi-worker broadcast fan-out using Redis Pub/Sub channels to distribute events across clustered Node.js processes
Writing efficient SQL window functions and continuous aggregate rollups in PostgreSQL to support fast historical interval slicing (1m, 5m, 1h, 24h)
Rendering dynamic 60 FPS live charts and animated metric counters in React without triggering unnecessary component re-renders or layout reflows
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating React dashboard views, Node.js WebSocket socket gateways, Redis Pub/Sub distributors, and PostgreSQL queries
High-concurrency benchmark report validating 2,000 concurrent WebSocket client connections receiving 1,000 event broadcasts per second with sub-35ms latency
Anti-fake verification script publishing a synthetic $10,000 transaction event and asserting the connected browser UI increments the total revenue counter within 100 milliseconds

architecture.data_flow: A transaction event posts to the ingestion API; Node.js writes the raw event to PostgreSQL; simultaneously, the server publishes a lightweight delta payload to the Redis 'metrics:updates' channel; all active Node.js worker processes receive the Redis message; each worker identifies connected WebSocket clients subscribed to that metric room; the worker serializes the JSON frame and broadcasts it over WebSockets in < 35ms; the React client receives the WebSocket message, updates its local state store, and smoothly re-renders the KPI card and live chart; when the user changes historical date ranges, the client fetches aggregated buckets from the PostgreSQL REST API.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Bounded WebSocket send buffers and client-side throttled requestAnimationFrame animation loops preventing UI freezes.

targets.method: Wall-clock timing from event ingestion POST request arrival to WebSocket frame delivery across 2,000 connected clients

targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Redis 7+ and PostgreSQL 15+ in Docker, Node.js 18+ runtime
targets.minimum_pass: p95 broadcast latency across connected clients is < 50.0 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 broadcast latency across connected clients is < 22.5 milliseconds
targets.report: WebSocket broadcast latency benchmark report and delivery percentile table

targets.method: Execution timing to query and assemble 24-hour hourly metric rollups across 1,000,000 historical records
targets.input: 100 repeated analytical SQL aggregation queries issued against database with 1,000,000 event rows
targets.environment: Local PostgreSQL 15+ instance with indexed timestamp and category columns
targets.minimum_pass: p95 historical query execution latency is < 65.0 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 historical query execution latency is < 24.0 milliseconds
targets.report: PostgreSQL query plan EXPLAIN ANALYZE log and execution duration table

targets.method: Sustained simultaneous WebSocket connections maintained without socket drops or memory exhaustion
targets.input: 2,000 headless WebSocket client connections established and maintained for 10 continuous minutes
targets.environment: Node.js WebSocket cluster on standard 4-core local CPU with 8GB RAM
targets.minimum_pass: Cluster sustains >= 2,000 active connections with 0 socket drops and RSS memory < 250MB
targets.target: Cluster sustains >= 3,500 active connections with 0 socket drops and RSS memory < 320MB
targets.report: WebSocket concurrency stress test report and memory usage trajectory

riskiest_component.name: WebSocket Slow-Consumer Buffer Bloat and Memory Leaks
riskiest_component.mitigation: Implement bounded client-side socket send buffers and automatically drop unacknowledged telemetry frames for lagging clients.
riskiest_component.fallback: Rate-limit broadcast frequencies to max 10 updates per second per client room.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a real-time business intelligence dashboard in TypeScript and React with Node.js WebSockets, Redis Pub/Sub, and PostgreSQL.
worksheet.q2: Target users: full-stack web developers, frontend systems architects, and real-time data platform engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: e-commerce flash-sale monitoring, fintech payment gateway anomaly ops, and SaaS ARR subscription metrics.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: 2,000 concurrent WebSocket connections, Redis Pub/Sub horizontal fan-out, fast PostgreSQL window rollups, and 60 FPS live rendering.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: React dashboard scaffolding, Node.js WebSocket gateway, Redis Pub/Sub wrapper, and PostgreSQL DDLs. Synthetic transaction data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU bound, $0 cost using Docker PostgreSQL and Redis.

worksheet.q9: Potential faking: polling REST APIs pretending to be real-time. Anti-fake check 5 publishes a $10,000 event and asserts WebSocket counter increment within 100ms.
worksheet.q10: Safe; synthetic financial records and private local Docker containers only.
